messages:
clara: Pushed a docs PR to update Boreas6B model card. Main items: clarify per-variant max sequence length (64k vs 128k), add embedding-shard caveats, and split the throughput bench by variant+quant. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/5059 :tada:

noel: nice. heard a customer hit strange embedding merge behavior with the 128k pro variant. can you call out which variants are safe for sharding and which need single-shard merges? :thinking:

clara: yes  draft lists: boreas6b-pro (fp16) = shardable, boreas6b-pro-128k (fp16, large-window) = shardable but requires "merge-buffer=large" flag; boreas6b-compact-int8 = non-shardable (merge issues). I'll add a Troubleshooting note with the exact merge command and link to embeddings troubleshooting doc.

samir: bench discrepancy question  your PR shows lower tokens/sec for the 128k runs vs our internal numbers. are those runs pinned-seqlen or variable? and which GPU? :eyes:

clara: good catch. the 128k numbers were using pinned-seqlen on A100-80GB with batch_size=1, fp16, and we accidentally reported the mixed avg with batch_size=4 runs. I'll split the table: pinned-seqlen A100-80GB (bs=1) row and variable-seq A100-40GB (bs=4) row. adding raw bench script link.

qa-lucy: add this checklist before merging: reproduce pinned 128k on A100-80GB, run tokenization diff on 200 prompts (lang+code), run embedding-shard idempotency test for the pro variant, and run a mem-smoke loop with 200 open/close contexts. I'll queue labs after PR is ready. ETA ~6h.

noel: SDK snippet request: show a short Python example for streaming generation on the 128k variant with graceful fallback to cpu for cold starts, and an embeddings snippet showing shard_hint. keep examples tiny.

clara: adding two snippets. generate snippet (streaming + fallback):

```python
from redwood import Client
client = Client(api_key="$REDWOOD_KEY")
resp = client.generate(
  model="boreas6b-pro-128k",
  input="Analyze log file and summarize anomalies:",
  stream=True,
  config={"fallback": "cpu"}
)
for chunk in resp.stream:
  print(chunk.text, end="")
```

embeddings snippet (shard hint):

```python
from redwood import Client
client = Client(api_key="$REDWOOD_KEY")
emb = client.embeddings.create(
  model="boreas6b-pro",
  input="customer support ticket text...",
  shard_hint="support:long"
)
print(len(emb.data[0].embedding))
```

noel: nit: change shard_hint taxonomy to "support:long" as you used, and link to https://docs.redwood.ai/embeddings/sharding. also call out that large-window variants may need higher merge-buffer.

doc-ci: lint report: models/boreas6b.md  headings OK; found 1 markdown-link warning (line 89) and 1 code-fence style warning (line 142).

clara: fixing the link and code fence style. assigning reviewers @noel @samir @qa-lucy. target to merge by tomorrow morning so it lands in the next catalog push. :calendar:

samir: I'll double-check the bench numbers and the bench script tomorrow AM. also can we include the raw perf command we ran (so customers can reproduce)?

clara: added the perf command under the bench table: `./perf/bench_run.sh --variant=boreas6b-pro-128k --gpu=A100-80 --seq=131072 --bs=1 --pinned`. included a short note about pinned vs variable seqlen effects.

qa-lucy: queuing the evals now; will post results here (expect ~5.5h). if embedding shard idempotency fails we'll block merge and open a follow-up doc+infra ticket. :warning:

noel: thanks all. small docs nit  update the "supported variants" summary at the top to reflect the non-shardable compact-int8 variant so sales/customer teams don't miss it.

clara: done, updated top-level summary and added a short "migration checklist" for customers moving to 128k windows (cache sizing, merge-buffer, and recommended runtime flags). tagging product and support. :white_check_mark:
